sanskrit: tasmāt tvam api viprebhyaḥ prayaccha kanakaṃ bahu dadat suvarṇaṃ nṛpate kilbiṣād vipramokṣyasi
english: Therefore do you too bestow abundant gold upon the brāhmaṇas; by giving gold, O king, you shall be released from all sin.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca uktāḥ pitāmaheneha suvarṇasya vidhānataḥ vistareṇa pradānasya ye guṇāḥ śrutilakṣaṇāḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The grandsire has set forth here at length, according to the ordinances, the virtues of the gift of gold as attested by the scriptures.

sanskrit: yat tu kāraṇam utpatteḥ suvarṇasyeha kīrtitam sa kathaṃ tārakaḥ prāpto nidhanaṃ tad bravīhi me
english: But touching the cause of the origin of gold that has been declared here—how did Tāraka meet his death? That tell me.

sanskrit: uktaḥ sa devatānāṃ hi avadhya iti pārthiva na ca tasyeha te mṛtyur vistareṇa prakīrtitaḥ
english: He was said to be unslayable by the gods, O lord of the earth; yet his death has not been recounted by you here in full.

sanskrit: etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ tvattaḥ kurukulodvaha kārtsnyena tārakavadhaṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
english: This I wish to hear from you, O upholder of the Kuru line—the slaying of Tāraka in its entirety; for great is my curiosity.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca vipannakṛtyā rājendra devatā ṛṣayas tathā kṛttikāś codayām āsur apatyabharaṇāya vai
english: Bhīṣma said: Their endeavour having failed, O king of kings, the gods and the sages alike urged the Kṛttikās to undertake the rearing of the child.

sanskrit: na devatānāṃ kā cid dhi samarthā jātavedasaḥ ekāpi śaktā taṃ garbhaṃ saṃdhārayitum ojasā
english: For not one among the goddesses was able by her own might to bear that embryo of Agni, the knower of all that is born.

sanskrit: ṣaṇṇāṃ tāsāṃ tataḥ prītaḥ pāvako garbhadhāraṇāt svena tejovisargeṇa vīryeṇa parameṇa ca
english: Then Pāvaka, the purifier, was pleased with those six for their bearing of the embryo, by reason of his own outpoured splendour and supreme potency.

sanskrit: tās tu ṣaṭ kṛttikā garbhaṃ pupuṣur jātavedasaḥ ṣaṭsu vartmasu tejo 'gneḥ sakalaṃ nihitaṃ prabho
english: Those six Kṛttikās nourished the embryo of Jātavedas; into their six channels was the whole splendour of Agni deposited, O lord.

sanskrit: tatas tā vardhamānasya kumārasya mahātmanaḥ tejasābhiparītāṅgyo na kva cic charma lebhire
english: Then, their limbs wholly compassed about by the splendour of that growing and high-souled boy, they could find ease nowhere.

sanskrit: tatas tejaḥparītāṅgyaḥ sarvāḥ kāla upasthite samaṃ garbhaṃ suṣuvire kṛttikās tā nararṣabha
english: Then, their limbs encompassed by that splendour, when the appointed time was come, all those Kṛttikās gave birth to the embryo together, O bull among men.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ ṣaḍadhiṣṭhānaṃ garbham ekatvam āgatam pṛthivī pratijagrāha kāntīpurasamīpataḥ
english: Then the Earth received that embryo, which from its six seats had come into oneness, near the city of Kāntī.

sanskrit: sa garbho divyasaṃsthāno dīptimān pāvakaprabhaḥ divyaṃ śaravaṇaṃ prāpya vavṛdhe priyadarśanaḥ
english: That embryo, of celestial form, blazing, bright as Pāvaka, having reached a divine thicket of reeds, grew up, fair to behold.

sanskrit: dadṛśuḥ kṛttikās taṃ tu bālaṃ vahnisamadyutim jātasnehāś ca sauhārdāt pupuṣuḥ stanyavisravaiḥ
english: The Kṛttikās beheld that child, splendid as fire; and tenderness arising, out of affection they nourished him with the flowing of their milk.

sanskrit: abhavat kārttikeyaḥ sa trailokye sacarācare skannatvāt skandatāṃ cāpa guhāvāsād guho 'bhavat
english: He became Kārttikeya throughout the three worlds, with all that moves and is unmoving; from his being poured forth he attained the state of Skanda, and from dwelling in a covert he became Guha.

sanskrit: tato devās trayastriṃśad diśaś ca sadigīśvarāḥ rudro dhātā ca viṣṇuś ca yajñaḥ pūṣāryamā bhagaḥ
english: Then the three-and-thirty gods, and the quarters with their guardian lords, Rudra and Dhātṛ and Viṣṇu, Yajña, Pūṣan, Aryaman, Bhaga,

sanskrit: aṃśo mitraś ca sādhyāś ca vasavo vāsavo 'śvinau āpo vāyur nabhaś candro nakṣatrāṇi grahā raviḥ
english: Aṃśa and Mitra and the Sādhyas, the Vasus, Vāsava, the two Aśvins, the Waters, Vāyu, the Sky, the Moon, the lunar mansions, the planets, the Sun—

sanskrit: pṛthag bhūtāni cānyāni yāni devārpaṇāni vai ājagmus tatra taṃ draṣṭuṃ kumāraṃ jvalanātmajam ṛṣayas tuṣṭuvuś caiva gandharvāś ca jagus tathā
english: and other separate beings, those that are offered in oblation to the gods, came there to behold that prince, the son of the flaming one; and the sages praised him, and the Gandharvas likewise sang.

sanskrit: ṣaḍānanaṃ kumāraṃ taṃ dviṣaḍakṣaṃ dvijapriyam pīnāṃsaṃ dvādaśabhujaṃ pāvakādityavarcasam
english: That prince of six faces and twice-six eyes, dear to the twice-born, broad-shouldered, twelve-armed, with the lustre of Fire and the Sun,

sanskrit: śayānaṃ śaragulmasthaṃ dṛṣṭvā devāḥ saharṣibhiḥ lebhire paramaṃ harṣaṃ menire cāsuraṃ hatam
english: as he lay couched within the reed-clump—beholding him, the gods together with the sages won the highest joy, and deemed the Asura already slain.

sanskrit: tato devāḥ priyāṇy asya sarva eva samācaran krīḍataḥ krīḍanīyāni daduḥ pakṣigaṇāṃś ca ha
english: Then the gods, every one of them, did all that was pleasing to him, and to him at his play they gave playthings and flocks of birds.

sanskrit: suparṇo 'sya dadau patraṃ mayūraṃ citrabarhiṇam rākṣasāś ca dadus tasmai varāhamahiṣāv ubhau
english: Suparṇa gave him for his vehicle a peacock with bright-hued plumage, and the Rākṣasas gave him both a boar and a buffalo.

sanskrit: kukkuṭaṃ cāgnisaṃkāśaṃ pradadau varuṇaḥ svayam candramāḥ pradadau meṣam ādityo rucirāṃ prabhām
english: Varuṇa himself bestowed a cock resembling fire; the Moon gave a ram, and the Sun a radiant splendour.

sanskrit: gavāṃ mātā ca gā devī dadau śatasahasraśaḥ chāgam agnir guṇopetam ilā puṣpaphalaṃ bahu
english: And the goddess, mother of cattle, gave kine by hundreds of thousands; Agni gave a goat endowed with good qualities, and Ilā much fruit and flower.

sanskrit: sudhanvā śakaṭaṃ caiva rathaṃ cāmitakūbaram varuṇo vāruṇān divyān bhujaṃgān pradadau śubhān siṃhān surendro vyāghrāṃś ca dvīpino 'nyāṃś ca daṃṣṭriṇaḥ
english: Sudhanvan gave a cart and a chariot with measureless pole; Varuṇa gave auspicious celestial serpents of his own kind; and Surendra gave lions and tigers and panthers and other fanged beasts.

sanskrit: śvāpadāṃś ca bahūn ghorāṃś chatrāṇi vividhāni ca rākṣasāsurasaṃghāś ca ye 'nujagmus tam īśvaram
english: and many fearsome beasts of prey, and parasols of various kinds; and hosts of Rākṣasas and Asuras there were who followed that lord.

sanskrit: vardhamānaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā prārthayām āsa tārakaḥ upāyair bahubhir hantuṃ nāśakac cāpi taṃ vibhum
english: But beholding him as he grew, Tāraka sought by many devices to slay him, yet he could not slay that mighty one.

sanskrit: senāpatyena taṃ devāḥ pūjayitvā guhālayam śaśaṃsur viprakāraṃ taṃ tasmai tārakakāritam
english: The gods, having honoured the dweller in the covert with the office of commander, told him of that outrage which Tāraka had wrought.

sanskrit: sa vivṛddho mahāvīryo devasenāpatiḥ prabhuḥ jaghānāmoghayā śaktyā dānavaṃ tārakaṃ guhaḥ
english: Then Guha, grown to full strength, of mighty valour, the lordly commander of the divine host, slew the Dānava Tāraka with his unfailing spear.

sanskrit: tena tasmin kumāreṇa krīḍatā nihate 'sure surendraḥ sthāpito rājye devānāṃ punar īśvaraḥ
english: When the Asura had been slain by that prince as though in sport, Surendra was once more established as lord upon the kingdom of the gods.

sanskrit: sa senāpatir evātha babhau skandaḥ pratāpavān īśo goptā ca devānāṃ priyakṛc chaṃkarasya ca
english: Then valorous Skanda shone forth as commander, the lord and protector of the gods, and a doer of what was dear to Śaṃkara.

sanskrit: hiraṇyamūrtir bhagavān eṣa eva ca pāvakiḥ sadā kumāro devānāṃ senāpatyam avāptavān
english: This same blessed one of golden form, the son of Pāvaka, ever a youth, attained to the generalship of the gods.

sanskrit: tasmāt suvarṇaṃ maṅgalyaṃ ratnam akṣayyam uttamam sahajaṃ kārttikeyasya vahnes tejaḥ paraṃ matam
english: Therefore gold is held auspicious, an imperishable and excellent jewel, born together with Kārttikeya, deemed the supreme splendour of Fire.

sanskrit: evaṃ rāmāya kauravya vasiṣṭho 'kathayat purā tasmāt suvarṇadānāya prayatasva narādhipa
english: Thus did Vasiṣṭha relate to Rāma of old, O Kaurava; therefore strive after the giving of gold, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: rāmaḥ suvarṇaṃ dattvā hi vimuktaḥ sarvakilbiṣaiḥ triviṣṭape mahat sthānam avāpāsulabhaṃ naraiḥ
english: For Rāma, having given gold, was freed of all his sins, and won in heaven a high place hard for men to attain.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca cāturvarṇyasya dharmātman dharmaḥ proktas tvayānagha tathaiva me śrāddhavidhiṃ kṛtsnaṃ prabrūhi pārthiva
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The duty of the four orders, O righteous one, has been declared by you, O sinless lord; even so now declare to me in full the rite of the śrāddha, O king.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca yudhiṣṭhireṇaivam ukto bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavas tadā imaṃ śrāddhavidhiṃ kṛtsnaṃ pravaktum upacakrame
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu then set about to expound this whole rite of the śrāddha.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śṛṇuṣvāvahito rājañ śrāddhakalpam imaṃ śubham dhanyaṃ yaśasyaṃ putrīyaṃ pitṛyajñaṃ paraṃtapa
english: Bhīṣma said: Hearken attentively, O king, to this auspicious ordinance of the śrāddha—wealth-giving, fame-bestowing, conducive to offspring, the sacrifice to the fathers, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: devāsuramanuṣyāṇāṃ gandharvoragarakṣasām piśācakiṃnarāṇāṃ ca pūjyā vai pitaraḥ sadā
english: By gods, Asuras, and men, by Gandharvas, serpents, and Rākṣasas, by Piśācas and Kiṃnaras, the fathers are ever to be honoured.

sanskrit: pitṝn pūjyāditaḥ paścād devān saṃtarpayanti vai tasmāt sarvaprayatnena puruṣaḥ pūjayet sadā
english: Having first honoured the fathers, men afterward satisfy the gods; therefore with all endeavour should a man honour them ever.

sanskrit: anvāhāryaṃ mahārāja pitṝṇāṃ śrāddham ucyate tac cāmiṣeṇa vidhinā vidhiḥ prathamakalpitaḥ
english: The śrāddha of the fathers, O great king, is called the anvāhārya; and its performance with flesh, by ordinance, was the rite first appointed.

sanskrit: sarveṣv ahaḥsu prīyante kṛtaiḥ śrāddhaiḥ pitāmahāḥ pravakṣyāmi tu te sarvāṃs tithyāṃ tithyāṃ guṇāguṇān
english: On all days are the fathers gladdened by the śrāddhas performed; yet I shall declare to you, for each lunar day, the merits and demerits of each.

sanskrit: yeṣv ahaḥsu kṛtaiḥ śrāddhair yat phalaṃ prāpyate 'nagha tat sarvaṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi yathāvat tan nibodha me
english: On whatsoever days the śrāddhas, when performed, yield what fruit, O sinless one—all this I shall duly recount; learn it of me.

sanskrit: pitṝn arcya pratipadi prāpnuyāt svagṛhe striyaḥ abhirūpaprajāyinyo darśanīyā bahuprajāḥ
english: Worshipping the fathers on the first lunar day, a man obtains in his own house women fair-formed, bearing comely offspring, lovely to look upon, and rich in children.

sanskrit: striyo dvitīyāṃ jāyante tṛtīyāyāṃ tu vandinaḥ caturthyāṃ kṣudrapaśavo bhavanti bahavo gṛhe
english: On the second are born daughters; on the third, panegyrists; on the fourth there come to be in the house many small cattle.

sanskrit: pañcamyāṃ bahavaḥ putrā jāyante kurvatāṃ nṛpa kurvāṇās tu narāḥ ṣaṣṭhyāṃ bhavanti dyutibhāginaḥ
english: On the fifth, to those who perform it, O king, are born many sons; and men who perform it on the sixth come to share in radiance.

sanskrit: kṛṣibhāgī bhavec chrāddhaṃ kurvāṇaḥ saptamīṃ nṛpa aṣṭamyāṃ tu prakurvāṇo vāṇijye lābham āpnuyāt
english: He who performs the śrāddha on the seventh becomes a sharer in the harvest, O king; performing it on the eighth, a man obtains gain in trade.

sanskrit: navamyāṃ kurvataḥ śrāddhaṃ bhavaty ekaśaphaṃ bahu vivardhante tu daśamīṃ gāvaḥ śrāddhāni kurvataḥ
english: To him who performs the śrāddha on the ninth come single-hooved beasts in plenty; and to him who performs the śrāddhas on the tenth, the kine increase.

sanskrit: kupyabhāgī bhaven martyaḥ kurvann ekādaśīṃ nṛpa brahmavarcasvinaḥ putrā jāyante tasya veśmani
english: A man who performs it on the eleventh becomes a sharer in base metals, O king; and sons radiant with sacred lore are born within his house.

sanskrit: dvādaśyām īhamānasya nityam eva pradṛśyate rajataṃ bahu citraṃ ca suvarṇaṃ ca manoramam
english: To him who strives at the rite on the twelfth there is ever seen abundant silver of varied kind, and gold delightful to the mind.

sanskrit: jñātīnāṃ tu bhavec chreṣṭhaḥ kurvañ śrāddhaṃ trayodaśīm avaśyaṃ tu yuvāno 'sya pramīyante narā gṛhe
english: Performing the śrāddha on the thirteenth, a man becomes foremost among his kinsmen; yet inevitably the young men of his house come to die.

sanskrit: yuddhabhāgī bhaven martyaḥ śrāddhaṃ kurvaṃś caturdaśīm amāvāsyāṃ tu nivapan sarvān kāmān avāpnuyāt
english: A man who performs the śrāddha on the fourteenth becomes a partaker in battle; but offering on the new-moon day, he obtains all his desires.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇapakṣe daśamyādau varjayitvā caturdaśīm śrāddhakarmaṇi tithyaḥ syuḥ praśastā na tathetarāḥ
english: In the dark fortnight, beginning with the tenth and excepting the fourteenth, the lunar days are commended for the rite of the śrāddha—not so are the others.

sanskrit: yathā caivāparaḥ pakṣaḥ pūrvapakṣād viśiṣyate tathā śrāddhasya pūrvāhṇād aparāhṇo viśiṣyate
english: And even as the latter fortnight is held superior to the former, so for the śrāddha is the afternoon superior to the forenoon.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kiṃ svid dattaṃ pitṛbhyo vai bhavaty akṣayam īśvara kiṃ haviś cirarātrāya kim ānantyāya kalpate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What gift made to the fathers becomes imperishable, O lord? What oblation avails for a long season, and what conduces to endlessness?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca havīṃṣi śrāddhakalpe tu yāni śrāddhavido viduḥ tāni me śṛṇu kāmyāni phalaṃ caiṣāṃ yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: The oblations in the rite of the śrāddha that the knowers of the śrāddha know—hear of me those that fulfil desire, and their fruit, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: tilair vrīhiyavair māṣair adbhir mūlaphalais tathā dattena māsaṃ prīyante śrāddhena pitaro nṛpa
english: With sesame, with rice and barley, with beans, with water, and with roots and fruits—by the śrāddha so offered the fathers are gladdened for a month, O king.

sanskrit: vardhamānatilaṃ śrāddham akṣayaṃ manur abravīt sarveṣv eva tu bhojyeṣu tilāḥ prādhānyataḥ smṛtāḥ
english: A śrāddha abounding in sesame is imperishable, Manu declared; and among all things that may be eaten, sesame is held to hold the foremost place.

sanskrit: dvau māsau tu bhavet tṛptir matsyaiḥ pitṛgaṇasya ha trīn māsān āvikenāhuś cāturmāsyaṃ śaśena tu
english: With fishes the satisfaction of the host of fathers lasts two months; with mutton, men say, three months; and with hare's flesh, four months.

sanskrit: ājena māsān prīyante pañcaiva pitaro nṛpa vārāheṇa tu ṣaṇmāsān sapta vai śākunena tu
english: With goat's flesh the fathers are gladdened five months, O king; with boar's flesh six months; and seven months with the flesh of fowl.

sanskrit: māsān aṣṭau pārṣatena rauraveṇa navaiva tu gavayasya tu māṃsena tṛptiḥ syād daśamāsikī
english: Eight months with the flesh of the spotted deer, and nine indeed with that of the ruru deer; and with the flesh of the gavaya the satisfaction lasts ten months.

sanskrit: māsān ekādaśa prītiḥ pitṝṇāṃ māhiṣeṇa tu gavyena datte śrāddhe tu saṃvatsaram ihocyate
english: With buffalo's flesh the fathers' contentment lasts eleven months; but when the śrāddha is offered with cow's milk and the like, it is said here to last a full year.

sanskrit: yathā gavyaṃ tathā yuktaṃ pāyasaṃ sarpiṣā saha vādhrīṇasasya māṃsena tṛptir dvādaśavārṣikī
english: As with the produce of the cow, so likewise is it with milk-rice joined with clarified butter; and with the flesh of the vādhrīṇasa the satisfaction lasts twelve years.

sanskrit: ānantyāya bhaved dattaṃ khaḍgamāṃsaṃ pitṛkṣaye kālaśākaṃ ca lauhaṃ cāpy ānantyaṃ chāga ucyate
english: Rhinoceros-flesh given at the offering to the fathers avails for endlessness; and the kālaśāka herb, and red goat, are said likewise to conduce to endlessness.

sanskrit: gāthāś cāpy atra gāyanti pitṛgītā yudhiṣṭhira sanatkumāro bhagavān purā mayy abhyabhāṣata
english: And here too they sing verses sung by the fathers, O Yudhiṣṭhira; the blessed Sanatkumāra of old spoke them unto me.

sanskrit: api naḥ sa kule jāyād yo no dadyāt trayodaśīm maghāsu sarpiṣā yuktaṃ pāyasaṃ dakṣiṇāyane
english: "May there be born in our line one who would offer us, on the thirteenth day, under the asterism Maghā, in the sun's southern course, milk-rice joined with clarified butter;

sanskrit: ājena vāpi lauhena maghāsv eva yatavrataḥ hasticchāyāsu vidhivat karṇavyajanavījitam
english: or with goat's flesh, or with red goat, under those very Maghās, one of steadfast vows, duly fanned with the ear-fan amid the shadows of elephants."

sanskrit: eṣṭavyā bahavaḥ putrā yady eko 'pi gayāṃ vrajet yatrāsau prathito lokeṣv akṣayyakaraṇo vaṭaḥ
english: Many sons should be desired, that even one of them might journey to Gayā, where stands renowned throughout the worlds that fig-tree which makes the offering imperishable.

sanskrit: āpo mūlaṃ phalaṃ māṃsam annaṃ vāpi pitṛkṣaye yat kiṃ cin madhusaṃmiśraṃ tad ānantyāya kalpate
english: Water, root, fruit, flesh, or food given at the offering to the fathers—whatsoever is mingled with honey conduces to endlessness.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca yamas tu yāni śrāddhāni provāca śaśabindave tāni me śṛṇu kāmyāni nakṣatreṣu pṛthak pṛthak
english: Bhīṣma said: The śrāddhas that Yama declared to Śaśabindu—hear of me those that fulfil desire, severally under each lunar mansion.

sanskrit: śrāddhaṃ yaḥ kṛttikāyoge kurvīta satataṃ naraḥ agnīn ādhāya sāpatyo yajeta vigatajvaraḥ
english: The man who should ever perform the śrāddha under the conjunction of the Kṛttikās, having set up the sacred fires, would sacrifice with offspring and free of fever.

sanskrit: apatyakāmo rohiṇyām ojaskāmo mṛgottame krūrakarmā dadac chrāddham ārdrāyāṃ mānavo bhavet
english: He who longs for offspring should offer under Rohiṇī; he who longs for vigour, under the lordly deer-mansion; but a man giving the śrāddha under Ārdrā becomes one of cruel deeds.

sanskrit: kṛṣibhāgī bhaven martyaḥ kurvañ śrāddhaṃ punarvasau puṣṭikāmo 'tha puṣyeṇa śrāddham īheta mānavaḥ
english: A man performing the śrāddha under Punarvasu becomes a sharer in the harvest; and one who longs for nourishment should strive at the śrāddha under Puṣya.

sanskrit: āśleṣāyāṃ dadac chrāddhaṃ vīrān putrān prajāyate jñātīnāṃ tu bhavec chreṣṭho maghāsu śrāddham āvapan
english: Giving the śrāddha under Āśleṣā, a man begets heroic sons; and offering the śrāddha under the Maghās, he becomes foremost among his kinsmen.

sanskrit: phalgunīṣu dadac chrāddhaṃ subhagaḥ śrāddhado bhavet apatyabhāg uttarāsu hastena phalabhāg bhavet
english: Giving the śrāddha under the Phalgunīs, the giver becomes blessed with fortune; under the Uttaras he becomes a sharer in offspring, and under Hasta a sharer in fruit.

sanskrit: citrāyāṃ tu dadac chrāddhaṃ labhed rūpavataḥ sutān svātiyoge pitṝn arcya vāṇijyam upajīvati
english: Giving the śrāddha under Citrā, he obtains comely sons; worshipping the fathers under the conjunction of Svāti, he lives by trade.

sanskrit: bahuputro viśākhāsu pitryam īhan bhaven naraḥ anurādhāsu kurvāṇo rājacakraṃ pravartayet
english: A man striving at the rite to the fathers under the Viśākhās becomes rich in sons; and performing it under the Anurādhās, he sets in motion the wheel of empire.

sanskrit: ādipatyaṃ vrajen martyo jyeṣṭhāyām apavarjayan naraḥ kurukulaśreṣṭha śraddhādamapuraḥsaraḥ
english: A man, O foremost of the Kuru line, going with faith and self-restraint before him, attains to sovereignty by making the offering under Jyeṣṭhā.

sanskrit: mūle tv ārogyam arccheta yaśo 'ṣāḍhāsv anuttamam uttarāsu tv aṣāḍhāsu vītaśokaś caren mahīm
english: Under Mūla he should attain health, and under the Aṣāḍhās fame unsurpassed; and under the Uttarāṣāḍhās, freed of sorrow, he would range the earth.

sanskrit: śrāddhaṃ tv abhijitā kurvan vidyāṃ śreṣṭhām avāpnuyāt śravaṇe tu dadac chrāddhaṃ pretya gacchet parāṃ gatim
english: Performing the śrāddha under Abhijit, he would obtain the highest knowledge; and giving the śrāddha under Śravaṇa, he would go after death to the supreme course.
